display.purpose: Main editor heading; reduces in size on narrow phones.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Border, background, and transform feedback on controls.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable transitions and smooth scrolling when requested.

breakpoints.name: compact-mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Tighten gutters and controls; make the primary action full width.

components.name: Primary action
components.description: Starts generation after a photo is selected.
components.css: .button { min-height:42px; border:0; border-radius:3px; background:#d7262d; color:#fff; padding:11px 17px; font-size:13px; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; transition:background .15s,transform .15s } .button:hover { background:#b91f26; transform:translateY(-1px) } .button:disabled { background:#aeb7c3; cursor:not-allowed; transform:none }

components.name: Edit choice
components.description: A single selectable photo treatment with a compact category tag.
components.css: .choice { width:100%; min-height:61px; border:1px solid #d5dbe3; background:#fff; color:#152442; border-radius:3px; padding:9px 11px; display:grid; grid-template-columns:18px minmax(0,1fr) auto; align-items:center; gap:10px; text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:border-color .15s,background .15s } .choice[aria-pressed="true"] { border:2px solid #d7262d; padding:8px 10px; background:#fffafa } .choice[aria-pressed="true"] .radio { border:4px solid #d7262d } .fare { color:#4b2e83; font:700 12px 'Barlow Condensed',sans-serif; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase }

components.name: Workspace panel
components.description: Flat white container for the source and controls or the edited result.
components.css: .panel { min-width:0; background:#fff; border:1px solid #d5dbe3; padding:19px; border-radius:4px }

components.name: Journey progress
components.description: Three numbered steps show photo, edit, and result progress.
components.html:
1 Add photo
2 Choose edit
3 Get result
components.css: .steps { min-height:72px; background:#fff; border-bottom:1px solid #d5dbe3; display:flex; align-items:center } .step { display:flex; align-items:center; flex:1; gap:10px; color:#59677d; font-size:13px } .step-number { width:25px; height:25px; display:grid; place-items:center; border:1px solid #aab6c5; border-radius:50%; font-size:11px } .step.current .step-number, .step.complete .step-number { background:#d7262d; border-color:#d7262d; color:#fff }

narrative.overview:
SafeFrame turns one photo edit into a short, legible trip: choose a source, select one treatment, and collect the finished image. The ticket-wallet reference contributes its navy and red identity, condensed display type, tab-like labels, crisp dividers, and a single three-step progress signature. The interface stays an ordinary photo tool; travel language is an organizing cue, not a layer of invented travel facts.

The two-panel workspace keeps the source and its compact edit controls together on the left while the result remains visible on the right from the first desktop view. The same hierarchy collapses into one mobile column, with the source and edit choices before the result. Privacy and creative modes share the same clear selection and action pattern.
keyCharacteristics: A short, ordered Choose → Edit → Ready journey.
A restrained carrier palette with red reserved for active progress and primary action.
Standard, legible photo controls inside a crisp, low-depth layout.

rules.name: The Two-Panel First View Rule
rules.body: Keep the source and compact edit controls together on the left, with the result pane visible on the right from the first desktop view.

rules.name: The Ticket Cue Rule
rules.body: Use travel language to organize the short edit journey; do not invent flight facts or let decorative travel details obscure photo controls.

dos: Do keep the desktop source-and-controls panel beside a visible result panel from the first view.
Do keep the three edit modes distinct and selectable before generation.
Do retain the visible focus treatment and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: Don't turn the editor into a feed, gallery, or stack of decorative upload cards.
Don't add invented flight information or travel facts to the ticket-wallet metaphor.
Don't obscure the selected photo, edit choice, generation state, or result download behind decorative travel details.
